title: Bilder und Artikel — das, die, der

paragraphs.text: The nine captions on this page give you more than a word each. Every noun arrives wearing one of three little words — {{de:das}}, {{de:die}} or {{de:der}} — and that article is part of the noun, exactly as much as its spelling is. English papers over the same difference with a single the; German keeps three, and it asks you to pick the right one every single time.

You cannot work the choice out from the meaning, so take it from the caption while the picture is in front of you: {{de:das Handtuch}}, {{de:die Flasche}}, {{de:der Koffer}}. Say the article aloud with the noun and the pair sticks together — and notice that German writes every noun with a capital letter, so the article is your earliest clue to where a word begins.
das Handtuch · die Flasche · der Koffer · das Würstchen · der Kindergarten · das Butterbrot · der Kranke · die Autobahn · die Nudeln

Nine captions are a small sample of a very large habit. From here on, every new noun in this book will be printed the same way, and the fastest speakers in your class will be the ones who started saying the three words together from day one.
